pages.text: $(o)A traveller's time is the length of its road, divided by its haste. A long road walked slowly leaves the most time behind.$()$(br2)$(7)(t = d / v)$()

Graft a $(l)Starting Gate$() onto a $(l)Speed$() organism and a $(l)Finish$() onto a $(l)Time$() organism, and join them with a vein. The gate sends a pulse of Speed down the vein; the time it spends on the road condenses at the finish: a dram for every two seconds.
pages.title: The Racetrack

pages.text: Use the gate with an empty hand to set its $(l)pace$(): slower pulses make more Time. But a pulse still travelling after thirty seconds $(l)stalls$(), dies, and $(l)clogs$() the vein. Cut the clot out with $(l)shears$().$(br2)Every launch costs Speed, more for a longer road: the veins feed on what passes.
pages.title: Pace and Stalls

pages.text: A vein running alongside $(l)Density$() flesh is $(l)heavy$(): pulses crawl through it at half pace. Coil the road through the cellar, weigh it down where you want it slow, and keep it just short of stalling.
pages.title: Tuning the Road
